R0197.title: Multi-Signature Wallet Social Engineering
R0197.definition: Attackers use social engineering (fake urgent proposals, impersonating team members) to trick multi-signature wallet signers into quickly approving malicious transactions.

references.title: Multisig Best Practices to Maximize Transaction Security - Polygon

R0197.description:
Multi-signature wallet social engineering targets DAO, foundation, and institutional treasury approval flows. Attackers forge urgent proposals, impersonate team members, create pressure, or send misleading transaction summaries to make multiple signers approve malicious transactions.

Multisig reduces single-key failure but does not prevent coordinated mistaken approvals. Governance needs transaction simulation, timelocks, permission tiers, and independent review.

Limitation: Requires knowledge of the target's organizational structure and decision-making process
R0197.influence: Socially engineered multisig approvals can drain DAO or institutional treasuries despite formal multi-party controls.

observables: Multi-sig wallets see multiple signers abnormally approving large or unknown-destination transactions within a short window
Governance proposals use urgent rhetoric and signature requests target unverified contract calls without simulation
Team member accounts initiate or approve proposals atypical of historical habits during abnormal hours
Multi-sig transaction calldata does not match the functionality described in the proposal summary
Signer devices or session sources show geographic or environmental shifts when approving sensitive transactions
